_comment: Clubs whose history is split across two spellings in the stored results,
with the variants that should be read as one team.
Cause: the 2026 seasons arrive from a different provider than the
historical ones, under a different name convention — usually stripped
accents or a dropped legal prefix. The resolver picks ONE spelling, so a
club with 68 matches of history is served the 4 rows of the current
season and falls under the five-match gate. Two fixtures were withheld
for this on 22 Aug alone (Slask v Widzew, Zurich v Basel), plus Piast v
Legia and Luzern v Lausanne earlier the same day.
Every entry below was read off the store's own name list and checked
pairwise. Deliberately NOT merged:
Stade Lausanne-Ouchy   a DIFFERENT club from FC Lausanne-Sport
Wisla / Wisla Plock    two different clubs (Krakow and Plock), and
neither has a historical variant stored
Wieczysta Krakow       newly promoted, no counterpart to merge with
FC Thun and FC Vaduz were left split on the same list until 1 Sep, on the
argument that folding them builds a tip on six-year-old form. That was an
assertion, so it was measured: across 68,341 replayed cards, bucketed by
how far back the rolling ten reaches, tip 1 grades 83.56% on a normal
window and 81.10% once the window reaches four years or more. Controlled
within each league — the deep windows cluster in the cups and the Scottish
lower divisions, which grade badly anyway — the drag is 1.47 points on an
equal-league average over 35 leagues. Real, one-directional, and small.
Against that: the alternative is not a fresher tip, it is NO tip. And the
gate makes the stale rows temporary — it deactivates the moment the club
has five current-season rows of its own, so the old form bridges the first
few weeks of a season and then stops being read at all.
Checked first: neither club has a cross-division rescue. SUI-CL holds two
rows in total, both from a 2021 playoff, so the store simply does not have
the Swiss second tier. Where an adjacent division IS stored, a merge is the
WRONG tool and must not be used — store._apply_merges runs inside
load_results, so a merged club clears min_matches and the cross-division
fallback never fires. Merging Coventry's 2000-01 Premier League rows onto
its 2026 promotion would suppress a fallback that reads last season.
A merge applies only where the served variant is BELOW the match gate, so
it can add a fixture the engine withheld and can never change one it
already prices. See store._apply_merges.
